summary:
Index page printed 611 (PDF 635). It continues **C** and covers most of **D**. Locators are **printed** pages: **add 24** for the PDF page.

**ConvNets (continued from the previous page).** Sub-entries: convolution operation 235–239 (PDF 259–263), max-pooling operation 239–241 (PDF 263–265), architecture patterns 268, 272–276, 280–282 (PDF 292, 296–300, 304–306), depthwise separable convolutions 278–280 (PDF 302–304), training from scratch on a small dataset 241 (PDF 265), visualizing filters 291–299 (PDF 315–323), visualizing intermediate activations 285–291 (PDF 309–315), class-activation heatmaps 299–306 and ViTs 282 (PDF 306). Separate entries: *convolution operation* 235–239, 550 (border effects and padding 238, strides 239), *convolution kernel* 237, *convolutional base* 257, *cost function* 9, *cross-attention layer* 447 and *cuDNN kernel* 280, 375.

**D.** *data augmentation* 242, 252 (PDF 266, 276). *data parallelism* 548, 549 (PDF 572–573). *DataParallel*. *Dataset object* 248, 356, 555. *decoders* 464, 509. **deep learning** 1 (PDF 25), with sub-entries: artificial intelligence, machine learning, and 2–3, 599 (PDF 26–27); overview of 8, 597 (PDF 32, 621); generative AI 11 (PDF 35); frameworks 61–62; limitations of 564–570, 605 (PDF 588–594, 629); network architectures 600–605; staying up to date 607–608. *Dense layers* 191 and many others. *deploying model* as a REST API 185, in a browser 187, on device 186. *depthwise separable convolution layers* 272–280. *derivatives* 41 (PDF 65). *diffusion models* 501, 509, 518–530 (PDF 542–554).

concepts.name: convolution operation (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 235–239, 550 (PDF 259–263, 574). Border effects and padding are at 238 and strides at 239.
concepts.intuition: The main explanation is in the introduction to ConvNets. Printed 550 is about distributing the computation.
concepts.technical: The max-pooling operation follows directly at 239–241 (PDF 263–265).
concepts.significance: It is the basic building block of every vision model in the book.
concepts.misconception: Printed 550 is not a second tutorial on convolution. It concerns data parallelism.

concepts.name: deep learning (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 1 (PDF 25). Its sub-entries span the whole book: overview 8, 597; limitations 564–570, 605; network architectures 600–605.
concepts.intuition: Read it as a table of contents for the book's central theme.
concepts.technical: The limitations pages (PDF 588–594) belong to chapter 19 on the future of AI.
concepts.significance: It points to the opening definition and to the critical reflection in the closing chapters.
concepts.example: Open PDF 588 to see where deep learning falls short.
concepts.misconception: The 'deep learning 1' locator is printed page 1, not PDF page 1.

concepts.name: diffusion models (index entry)
concepts.definition: Indexed at printed 501, 509, 518–530 (PDF 525, 533, 542–554). Sub-entries for the diffusion schedule (524) and the generation process (527) continue on the next index page.
concepts.intuition: The full implementation, trained on Oxford Flowers, is at PDF 542–554.
concepts.technical: Related entries: denoise() method 527, DiffusionModel class 525.
concepts.significance: It is the book's modern image-generation technique.
concepts.example: Open PDF 548 for the diffusion schedule.
concepts.misconception: Not every locator is a full treatment. Printed 501 falls in the LLM pages (near the RAG entry), so it is probably a passing mention.
